articles.title: BMW M 1000 RS Unveiled at EICMA 2026: 218 hp, 1,000 Units
articles.excerpt: BMW Motorrad has unveiled the M 1000 RS at EICMA 2026: a 218 hp, 196 kg naked motorcycle limited to 1,000 units, priced at 40,000 euros in Germany, with deliveries from March 2027.
blocks: BMW Motorrad unveiled the **M 1000 RS** at the EICMA motorcycle show in Milan, reported on 3 November 2026. It uses the 999cc inline-four from the M 1000 RR superbike, makes 218hp, and weighs 196kg ready to ride, according to Autocar India and motorcycles.news. Production is limited to 1,000 units worldwide, the German price is 40,000 euros including VAT, and dealer deliveries start in March 2027. This article is current as of 3 November 2026.

Engine: 999cc water-cooled inline-four with BMW ShiftCam, taken from the M 1000 RR
Power: 218hp (160kW) at 14,500rpm
Torque: 113Nm at 11,000rpm
Kerb weight: 196kg ready to ride with a full tank
BMW's claimed 0 to 100 km/h: 3.2 seconds
BMW's claimed top speed: 283 km/h
Transmission: six-speed gearbox with chain final drive
The acceleration and top-speed numbers are manufacturer claims, not independent measurements.

According to motorcycles.news, the RS has an aluminium bridge frame that uses the engine as a load-bearing part, a 45mm upside-down fork and an aluminium swingarm with a central shock. Suspension is electronically controlled, with Dynamic Damping Control. The front brakes are radial four-piston calipers on two 320mm discs, and the rear has a 220mm disc. ABS Pro and traction control are standard.
Carbon wheels and a titanium exhaust come as standard, and the bike has small carbon winglets. Autocar India and motorcycles.news both list these items.

6.5-inch TFT display
Riding modes, adjustable traction control and cruise control
Keyless ride and tyre pressure monitoring
Heated grips (listed by motorcycles.news)
Options include a low screen, handlebar risers, alternative seats and M Performance Parts such as a data logger with a GPS lap trigger

Motorcycles.news gives the price as 40,000 euros including VAT in Germany and 36,220 pounds in the UK. Autocar India reports the German price and converts it to about Rs 42.36 lakh, but that is a currency conversion, not an Indian price. Neither source gives an Indian price or Indian launch plan, and motorcycles.news says prices for other markets have not been announced.
Deliveries through BMW Motorrad dealers begin in March 2027, and only 1,000 units will be built.
How it compares with the M 1000 R

The RS sits beside the M 1000 R naked motorcycle, which uses a related engine. The two sources give different power figures for the M 1000 R: Autocar India says 205hp at 13,000rpm, while motorcycles.news says 210hp at 13,750rpm. Both agree that the RS's 218hp is the higher output. Torque is about the same, 113Nm for the RS and about 112 to 113Nm for the R according to the two sources.

Motorcycles.news lists the RS at 196kg against 199kg for the M 1000 R, and a seat height of 850mm, 20mm higher than the R's 830mm. It adds that the RS name refers to the German word Rennsport, meaning racing, not the meaning used on the R 1300 RS.

BMW has not announced an Indian price or an Indian availability date in the reports read for this article. Prices in other countries are also not yet public. Anyone interested should wait for BMW Motorrad India's own announcement.

EICMA is the international motorcycle exhibition held every year in Milan, Italy, where makers often show new models before they reach showrooms. A "claimed" figure is one the maker states; it has not been measured by an independent tester. A "kerb weight" or "ready to ride" weight normally includes fluids and a full fuel tank, but the exact definition differs between makers, which is one reason weight figures from different companies cannot always be compared directly.

Horsepower figures also come in different units. Metric horsepower (PS) and mechanical horsepower (hp or bhp) differ by about 1.4 per cent, and kilowatts are a third way of stating the same power. BMW's 218hp is given alongside 160kW, which is consistent with the usual conversion. Where two outlets quote slightly different numbers for the same bike, the unit is often the reason, but the sources should be read before assuming so.
What the numbers tell you, and what they do not

The published figures describe the bike as BMW built it for the European market. They do not say how the motorcycle behaves on a road or track, because nobody outside the company has ridden it in the reports used here. This article therefore compares only numbers: the RS makes more power than the M 1000 R and weighs less, according to motorcycles.news, and it is limited to 1,000 units.

articles.title: Suzuki GSX-10R Unveiled at EICMA 2026: Specs and Dates
articles.excerpt: Suzuki has unveiled the GSX-10R, a 999cc inline-four sportbike, and the SV-7S naked bike at EICMA 2026. Sales start from spring 2027; no prices have been announced.
blocks: Suzuki unveiled the **GSX-10R** sportbike and the **SV-7S** naked bike at EICMA 2026 in Milan, according to Suzuki's global news page dated 3 November 2026. The GSX-10R is a fully faired bike with a 999cc inline-four and a claimed kerb weight of 214kg. Sales begin in various countries from summer 2027 for the GSX-10R and spring 2027 for the SV-7S. Suzuki has not announced prices. This article is current as of 3 November 2026.
Suzuki's page for the European specification gives these figures for the GSX-10R:

Engine: K5, 999cc liquid-cooled inline-four, DOHC
Kerb weight: 214kg
Wheelbase: 1,455mm; seat height: 810mm; ground clearance: 145mm
Tyres: 120/70ZR17 front, 190/55ZR17 rear
Fuel tank: 18 litres
Length, width, height: 2,130mm, 740mm, 1,175mm

Suzuki's page, as read for this article, does not list power or torque. Visordown reports a claimed 150bhp at 11,000rpm and 78lb-ft of torque at 9,250rpm. Autocar India gives 152hp and 106Nm. These are almost certainly the same figures in different units (152 PS is about 150bhp, and 78lb-ft is about 106Nm), though the sources do not say so.

Suzuki says the bike has its S.I.R.S. electronics package with 15 functions. The company's page names Slide Control, Brake Hold Control, Cruise Control, a bi-directional quick shift, Launch Control and the Suzuki Ground Beacon System, along with a colour TFT display. Visordown notes that Slide Control is a first for a Suzuki bike.

On the chassis, Visordown lists an aluminium twin-spar frame with a new aluminium swingarm, KYB suspension with fully adjustable 43mm inverted forks, twin front discs with a radial master cylinder, and Bridgestone Battlax Hypersport S23 tyres. It also reports a claimed maximum lean angle of 53 degrees.
How it relates to other Suzuki bikes

Autocar India says the engine is shared with other K5-based Suzuki models, and Visordown describes it as based on the K5 GSX-R1000 architecture, refined through the GSX-S1000. The GSX-R1000R remains in the range. Autocar India gives that bike 195hp, so the GSX-10R's claimed output is lower, while its claimed torque is only slightly below.

The SV-7S is a naked street bike with a 645cc liquid-cooled V-twin, ride-by-wire throttle, a claimed kerb weight of 200kg and a seat height of 785mm, according to Suzuki's page. Its electronics include three levels of the Suzuki Drive Mode Selector, three-mode traction control, a bi-directional quick shift and a 4.2-inch colour TFT. It has a 14-litre fuel tank.

Suzuki's page gives summer 2027 for the GSX-10R and spring 2027 for the SV-7S, in various countries. Visordown says Suzuki included no UK price or availability in its launch information. Autocar India says the GSX-10R is unlikely to come to India, but that is the outlet's view, not a Suzuki statement; Suzuki has not announced any India plan. Estimates of prices elsewhere are guesses and are not used here.
Specifications on this page are for the European models as published by Suzuki and Visordown. Figures for other markets may differ.

EICMA is the international motorcycle exhibition held every year in Milan, Italy, where makers often show new models before they reach showrooms. A "claimed" figure is one stated by the maker or reported from its launch material; it has not been measured by an independent tester. Kerb weight normally means the bike with fluids and a full tank, but definitions vary between makers, so weights from different companies are not always directly comparable.

Power appears in several units. Metric horsepower (PS) and mechanical horsepower (hp or bhp) differ by about 1.4 per cent, and torque is quoted in newton-metres (Nm) or pound-feet (lb-ft). Autocar India and Visordown quote the GSX-10R in different units, which is the likely reason their figures differ slightly. Suzuki's own European page, as read for this article, does not state power at all.
What the numbers tell you, and what they do not

Everything above describes the bikes on paper, as published at the show. None of the reports used here is a ride review, so nothing is known from them about how either bike feels to use. The GSX-10R's published figures place it below the GSX-R1000R on claimed power, according to Autocar India, but the sources do not say how Suzuki will position the price of either bike.

articles.title: Moto Guzzi The Trip 500 Unveiled at EICMA 2026
articles.excerpt: Moto Guzzi has shown The Trip, a new 500 roadster with a parallel-twin engine of almost 48 hp, at EICMA 2026. Price and exact dates have not been announced.
blocks: Moto Guzzi presented **The Trip**, a new 500cc roadster, at EICMA 2026 in Milan, according to the show's own website and Motorbox. It has a parallel-twin engine, which is new for the brand, a declared output of almost 48hp that fits the A2 licence limit, and a declared weight of 180kg in running order. Moto Guzzi has not announced a price. This article is current as of 3 November 2026.

Engine: 500cc parallel-twin
Power: almost 48hp, as declared by the manufacturer (within A2 licence limits)
Weight: 180kg in running order, declared by the manufacturer
Seat height: 790mm
Fuel tank: 15 litres
Gearbox: six-speed, with quick shifter
Frame: newly developed steel frame
Torque figures were not given in either source. Motorbox says the manufacturer states most of the torque is available at low revs, with full values to follow in the complete technical sheet.

The EICMA page lists upside-down front forks and a pair of adjustable rear shock absorbers. The bike has three riding modes: Road, Sport and Rain. A 3.6-inch circular TFT display can connect to a smartphone, and the switchgear is backlit. Neither source states the brake or wheel specification.

The Trip comes in three colours: Green Grove, Black Metropolis and Red Beat. A special edition called The Opening will mark the debut of the new generation of Moto Guzzi motorcycles. Motorbox says the company has not yet disclosed what extra equipment it carries.
Why it matters to the brand

The EICMA page describes The Trip as the start of a new generation for Moto Guzzi. The company is best known for its V-twin engines mounted across the frame, so a parallel-twin is a different layout. The sources do not name the engine's origin or say whether it is shared with another maker, so this article does not guess.

The EICMA page says the bike will reach dealers in early 2027. Motorbox says that availability and price have not yet been announced and notes only that it was shown at the Moto Guzzi stand in Pavilion 9. The two sources differ on availability, so treat the early 2027 date as the show page's statement until the company confirms it. Prices circulating online are estimates, not company figures, and are not repeated here.
Neither source mentions India. Moto Guzzi has not announced an Indian price or launch date for The Trip in the information read for this article.

EICMA is the international motorcycle exhibition held every year in Milan, Italy, where makers often show new models before they reach showrooms. A "declared" figure is one stated by the maker; it has not been measured independently. "Running order" weight normally means the bike with fluids and fuel but without a rider, though the exact definition differs between makers.

The A2 licence is a European category for riders stepping up from the smallest motorcycles. It limits a bike's power, and Moto Guzzi's page says the almost 48hp of The Trip falls within that limit. Rules for licence categories differ by country, and the Indian licensing system is different, so this statement relates to European rules.
What the numbers tell you, and what they do not

The reports available describe a motorcycle as it was shown at a stand, not as it is sold. Final specifications can change before sales start, and the manufacturer has said that a complete technical sheet is still to come, according to Motorbox. Torque, brakes, wheels and price are all missing from the sources read for this article, so none of them is stated here.
